role: independent exploration: menu legibility (the 7B misreads split counts)
hypothesis: The parent's wasted queries come from the 7B misreading the menu, not from the menu's content. Each option said 'n1 candidates say 1, n0 say 0', and the model's stated reasons show it reading this backwards (i0 call 3: 'highest imbalance'). Across the 10 parent traces it took the top option in 44/129 picks, and 21 picks were off-menu or re-asked. If each option instead carries ONE number where bigger is better (candidates GUARANTEED to be ruled out = min(n1,n0)), sorted biggest first, then (a) top-option picks rise well above 34% and off-menu/malformed replies fall, and (b) as a consequence queries/episode fall below the parent's 12.9. Falsified if (a) holds but (b) does not, which would mean the bottleneck is the ranking metric, not the model's reading.
behavior_changes: Menu lines read '<X>(a,b,c): rules out at least M of the N candidates for X' instead of 'n1 candidates say 1, n0 say 0'; the header says the number is guaranteed whatever the answer and bigger is better.

Menu sorted by min(n1,n0) descending (ties broken by per-circuit split entropy, then circuit/row) instead of by entropy alone; within one circuit the order is unchanged, but across circuits big circuits now come first.
Ask prompt: 'the one that rules out the most candidates is best' replaces 'that helps most'.
preserved_behaviors: Rule-derived candidate space (two AND/OR gates per circuit plus NOTs, inventory split without replacement) and the relaxed fallback if answers contradict it.
Model writes every query; same 8-option menu size (no truncation), same vetoes for malformed, repeated, solved-circuit and zero-information replies, same MAX_TRIES and temperatures.
Stop once every circuit has one candidate; final 24 bits assembled from the model's numbered per-circuit picks.
verification: Ran check_b2r0_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b2r0g1.py on the 10 instances: 10/10 status=ok, 10/10 parsed final guess, 0 crashes. Queries used 11,16,14,13,12,15,15,13,13,8 (mean 13.0, max 16) vs parent's 12.9 mean, max 17. Solver calls 140 vs parent 156.
Final-phase prompt in all 10 episodes shows every circuit SOLVED (one rule-consistent table each), with no '?' (relaxed) expressions, so no answer contradicted the rule model.

Parsed every query turn from the traces: top-option picks 80/130 (62%) vs parent 44/129 (34%); off-menu or malformed replies 0 vs 21; picks strictly weaker than the top option 7 vs about 30. Part (a) is confirmed.

Part (b) is NOT confirmed: mean queries did not drop. Label-free floor check: ceil(log2 #joint rule-consistent (A,B,C) tables) is 12 for the 1AND/5OR/2NOT and 3AND/3OR/1NOT inventories and 8 for 3AND/3OR. Episodes use 13-16 on the floor-12 instances, so the remaining 1-4 query gap sits in the per-circuit, unweighted ranking metric (it ignores inventory coupling between circuits), not in how the model reads the menu.
Did not consult gold/outcome fields; correctness of the final tables is not judged here beyond rule-consistency.
risks: min(n1,n0) ordering favours large circuits over a more even split on a small circuit; per step this can carry slightly less information than the parent's entropy order, which could offset the compliance gain (mean 13.0 vs 12.9 is within noise at n=10).
Instance 238 used 16/18; with a less lucky answer sequence a 3AND/3OR/1NOT instance could still approach the budget, because the metric still ignores the joint coupling.
Higher compliance makes the harness more dependent on its own ranking: if the rule model is wrong, the model follows a misleading menu more faithfully.
Natural combination to test next: this legible single-number wording with a joint-space ranking (sibling b1r1 lineage), which addresses the gap this run identifies.
